name: Postlingual Non-Syndromic Genetic Deafness

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic and Audiological Diagnostic Criteria for Postlingual Non-Syndromic Deafness

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with non-syndromic hearing loss
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss with postlingual onset confirmed by audiometry
Absence of clinical features indicating syndromic forms of deafness
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Normal inner ear imaging excluding structural abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral postlingual sensorineural hearing loss with genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants and exclusion of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing panels targeting known deafness genes are essential for confirmation.

searchTerms: hearing loss in both ears after childhood
bilateral sensorineural deafness after language development
both ears losing hearing after early years

common.symptomName: Difficulty understanding speech in noisy environments
searchTerms: trouble understanding speech with background noise
no dizziness related to inner ear
problems telling where sounds come from

rare.notes: Very rare and usually related to severe hearing loss
searchTerms: brief hearing of sounds not present

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying pathogenic variants in genes such as GJB2, TECTA, or MYO6
imaging: Normal temporal bone MRI and CT scans excluding structural abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with autosomal dominant or recessive non-syndromic hearing loss
other: Pure tone audiometry demonstrating bilateral sensorineural hearing loss with postlingual onset

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of additional systemic features such as pigmentation abnormalities, renal anomalies, or vestibular dysfunction
Genetic mutations associated with syndromic forms (e.g., Usher syndrome, Waardenburg syndrome)
History of ototoxic drug exposure, noise trauma, infections or autoimmune inner ear disease

redFlags: Presence of vestibular symptoms such as vertigo or imbalance
Additional systemic abnormalities suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Smith RJH, et al. Genetic Hearing Loss: Clinical and Molecular Aspects. Cold Spring Harb Perspect Med. 2015.
Orphanet: Postlingual Non-Syndromic Genetic Deafness. ORPHA:216452.
Shearer AE, Smith RJH. Genetics: Advances in Genetic Testing for Hearing Loss. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2015.
